title: MCP and Backend Integration
description: Understand how Model Context Protocol fits into backend architecture and why it is different from REST APIs for AI clients.

blocks.text: Model Context Protocol is an open protocol for connecting AI systems to backend capabilities. Instead of building a custom wrapper around every REST endpoint, an MCP server exposes resources, prompts, and tools in a standardized form that many AI clients can understand directly.

Traditional REST APIs return JSON, but they do not describe their capabilities in a way that an LLM can reliably use. MCP solves this by adding a machine-readable description layer: the client learns what tools exist, what inputs they expect, and what outputs they return.

blocks.title: What MCP adds beyond REST
items: **Capability discovery** — clients can inspect available tools and resources at runtime.
**Structured tool descriptions** — parameter types, enums, and descriptions that improve tool selection.
**Prompt templates** — reusable prompt fragments with arguments that the client can fill.
**Standardized transport** — stdio for local processes and HTTP/SSE for remote services.

blocks.content: An MCP server exposing a weather lookup tool that an AI client can discover and call.

blocks.title: MCP is complementary
blocks.text: MCP does not replace REST. Use REST for web clients and MCP where AI clients need structured discovery, tool use, or prompt templates.

items.text: I can explain why REST alone is hard for AI clients
items.hint: No standard schema, weak tool selection, and no prompt discovery

items.text: I know when to add MCP alongside REST
items.hint: When AI clients need tool calling, prompt templates, or dynamic capability discovery

items.text: I can name three MCP primitives

blocks.title: Lesson Summary
points: MCP standardizes how backends expose AI-ready capabilities.
It is most valuable for AI clients, not a replacement for REST.
C# backends can host MCP servers that wrap existing business logic.
blocks.takeaway: Treat MCP as an AI-native interface layer on top of your existing backend, not a full replacement.
